input.quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale: Two material gaps. First, Section 14 (p0079) never granted Client a termination right in operative terms: it only imposed a wind-down obligation on TrueLink running to a date fixed by "Client's election", so our convenience exit had to be inferred. We have recast it as a direct grant — "Client may terminate this Agreement for convenience, without cause, upon written notice to TrueLink" — while keeping the existing end-of-following-month wind-down (roughly 30–60 days, inside and better than the 60–90 day fallback ceiling) and the "subject to Section 4" qualifier. Second, Section 13 (p0078) auto-renews the one-year term but let TrueLink block renewal on only thirty (30) days' notice, a Vendor no-cause exit on fewer than 90 days' notice, which is the playbook's walk-away band and leaves no realistic migration window for hosting, interface and credit-data services; we now require ninety (90) days from TrueLink while preserving Client's favourable 30-day notice. No early-termination fee, penalty or unamortised charge exists anywhere — fees are charged per monthly invoice under Section 5(a) (p0045) — so the three-month cap is bettered. Sections 4 (p0043) and 12 (p0070–p0077) contain no TrueLink at-will exit or termination charge. This lands at the fallback; preferred is not claimed, as there is still no flat 30-day effective date and no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. Two tidy-ups for a follow-up pass: the stale "Section 12 herein" cross-reference (termination is Section 14) and the blank Section 4 minimum support period.

proposal.summary: Recast Section 14 as a direct Client right to terminate for convenience on written notice, and require 90 days' notice for TrueLink's end-of-term non-renewal.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have recast Section 14 as a direct right for Client to terminate for convenience, without cause, on written notice, keeping the existing wind-down date and the Section 4 qualifier, and we require TrueLink to give ninety (90) days' notice if it will not renew so its only no-cause exit remains the end of a term. Our own 30-day non-renewal notice is unchanged.

ops.oldText: Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
ops.newText: Client may terminate this Agreement for convenience, without cause, upon written notice to TrueLink, and, subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month of such notice.

ops.oldText: unless either Client or TrueLink deliver to the other written notice of intent not to renew no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year
ops.newText: unless Client delivers to TrueLink written notice of intent not to renew no later than thirty (30) days, or TrueLink delivers such notice no later than ninety (90) days, prior to the end of said year
